facts.statement: The genus Prognathodon was described by Louis Dollo in 1889.
facts.quote: authority: Dollo, 1889

facts.statement: Fossils of Prognathodon date from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Campanian - Maastrichtian,

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Prognathodon solvayi.
facts.quote: type_species: Prognathodon solvayi

facts.statement: Former names for Prognathodon include Prognathosaurus, Dollosaurus, Brachysaurana, Ancylocentrum, Tenerasaurus, Tylosaurus capensis, and Taniwhasaurus capensis.
facts.quote: synonyms: * Prognathosaurus (Dollo, 1889) (Williston, 1897) Dollosaurus (Yakovlev, 1905) Brachysaurana (Strand, 1926) Ancylocentrum (Schmidt, 1927) Tenerasaurus (Kaddumi, 2009) Tylosaurus capensis (Broom, 1912) Taniwhasaurus capensis (Broom, 1912)

facts.statement: Prognathodon belongs to the Mosasaurinae subfamily, which also includes Mosasaurus and Clidastes.
facts.quote: It is classified as part of the Mosasaurinae subfamily, alongside genera like Mosasaurus and Clidastes.

facts.statement: Prognathodon fossils have been found in the Middle East, Europe, New Zealand, Africa, and North America from the Campanian to Maastrichtian ages.
facts.quote: Prognathodon has been recovered from deposits ranging in age from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian in the Middle East, Europe, New Zealand, Africa and North America.

facts.statement: The name Prognathodon translates to "forejaw tooth" from Latin and Greek roots.
facts.quote: Prognathodon means "forejaw tooth", which originates from the Latin pro- ("earlier" or "prior"), Greek gnathos ("jaw") and odṓn ("tooth").

facts.statement: Prognathodon is characterized by its massively built jaws and teeth.
facts.quote: Prognathodon is known for its massively built jaws and teeth.

facts.statement: Prognathodon was first described in 1889 based on specimens collected in Belgium.
facts.quote: Prognathodon was first described by Louis Dollo in 1889 based on specimens gathered in Belgium.

facts.statement: An intact fossil skull of Prognathodon was discovered in 1998 in the Maastricht limestone quarries.
facts.quote: In 1998, an intact fossil skull was found in the Maastricht limestone quarries.

facts.statement: The Prognathodon saturator specimen from Maastricht is approximately 12 meters long and is displayed at the Natural History Museum at Maastricht.
facts.quote: This specimen was the first reasonably complete mosasaur specimen recovered from the Maastricht area since 1957; the skeleton is on display at the Natural History Museum at Maastricht, and is from an animal that was probably 12 metres long.

facts.statement: In 2009, P. hudae was described by Hani F. Kaddumi from fossils found in the Muwaqqar Chalk Marl Formation of Harrana, Jordan.
facts.quote: In 2009, Hani F. Kaddumi described the new species P. hudae based on a complete right dentary and partial left dentary from the Maastrichtian-age Muwaqqar Chalk Marl Formation of Harrana, Jordan.

facts.statement: P. primus was described in 2009 based on an articulated upper skull, representing the first near-complete mosasaur skull found in the Middle East.
facts.quote: Also described in 2009 by Kaddumi from the same locality was P. primus, based on an articulated upper skull, with the name referencing it being the first near-complete mosasaur skull from the Middle East.

facts.statement: A 1.8-meter-long juvenile Prognathodon fossil preserves the outline of a bilobed tail fluke resembling a shark's tail.
facts.quote: This fossil is about 1.8 m in length, and is remarkable in that it preserves the outline of the mosasaur's tail fins, revealing that Prognathodon had a bilobed tail fluke resembling a downturned shark's tail.

facts.statement: The "Carlo" specimen is considered the oldest known Mosasaurid from the Maastricht area and belongs to Prognathodon.
facts.quote: From what has been uncovered, this appears to be the oldest known Mosasaurid specimen from the Maastricht area, and it belongs to the genus Prognathodon.

facts.statement: Studies of preserved teeth and gut contents have helped infer the paleoecology of Prognathodon.
facts.quote: The preserved teeth and gut contents also allowed studies into the inferred paleoecology of the genus.

facts.statement: The systematics of Prognathodon and the validity of its species are controversial due to specimen differences and incompleteness.
facts.quote: Due to the sometimes clear differences between them and the incomplete nature of many of the specimens, the systematics of the genus and which species should properly be considered Prognathodon is controversial.

facts.statement: It is debated whether certain species should be assigned to genera like Dollosaurus and Brachysaurana rather than Prognathodon.
facts.quote: Some species have been assigned to other genera, such as Dollosaurus and Brachysaurana, but this has also been questioned.

facts.statement: A 2022 study suggested T. capensis is a chimera of Prognathodon and Taniwhasaurus, though it remains unidentifiable at the species level.
facts.quote: An anatomical review of South African mosasaurs by Woolley et al. (2022) reclassified T. capensis, originally assigned to Tylosaurus and later to Taniwhasaurus, as a chimera of two different mosasaur genera (cf. Prognathodon and cf. Taniwhasaurus), but not identifiable at the species level.

facts.statement: Very few Prognathodon specimens have articulated skulls, and no complete skeletons are known.
facts.quote: To date, very few specimens are known with articulated skulls and none with an entire skeleton.

facts.statement: In 1967, P. giganteus was estimated to reach 10 meters in length.
facts.quote: In 1967, P. giganteus was estimated to have reached 10 m in length.

facts.statement: In 2002, Christiansen and Bonde estimated the maximum length of P. currii at 11 meters.
facts.quote: In 2002, Christiansen and Bonde estimated the maximum length of P. currii at 11 m.

facts.statement: P. hudae is estimated to have reached 6.4 meters in length.
facts.quote: P. hudae is estimated to have reached 6.4 m in length.

facts.statement: The largest known P. overtoni specimen measures over 7 to 8 meters in length.
facts.quote: The largest P. overtoni specimen is TMP 2018.042.0005, a nearly completely preserved individual measuring over 7 - 8 m in length.

facts.statement: P. sectorius is estimated to have approached 8 meters in length.
facts.quote: P. sectorius would have approached the same size, about 8 m in length.

facts.statement: In P. solvayi, the scleral ring is partially preserved and consists of five scleral ossicles per ring.
facts.quote: In the type species, P. solvayi, the scleral ring is only partially preserved, consisting of five scleral ossicles in each ring.

facts.statement: Prognathodon is characterized by a very robust skull.
facts.quote: Prognathodon is noted as having a very robust skull.

facts.statement: The ratio of supratemporal fenestra length to total skull length is relatively high in Prognathodon (0.22 in P. overtoni and P. saturator) compared to Mosasaurus (0.19 in M. hoffmannii).
facts.quote: The ratio between the length of the supratemporal fenestra and the total length of the skull has previously been used as an improvised measurement for mosasaur bite force, and is relatively high in Prognathodon (0.22 in P. overtoni and P. saturator) compared to other genera, such as Mosasaurus (0.19 in M. hoffmannii).

facts.statement: The quadrates of Prognathodon have fused suprastapedial and infrastapedial processes, possibly an adaptation to withstand strong biting forces.
facts.quote: The quadrates of Prognathodon, similarly to the genus Globidens, have fused suprastapedial and infrastapedial processes, which is possibly an adaptation to counteract the strong forces experienced by the bone during biting.

facts.statement: The marginal teeth of Prognathodon are massive, smooth, and rounded, unlike the typically facetted and laterally compressed teeth of most other mosasaurs.
facts.quote: The marginal teeth are massive, smooth and rounded as opposed to most other mosasaur teeth, which are typically facetted and laterally compressed.

facts.statement: Some researchers classify P. lutugini in its own genus, Dollosaurus, while others place it within Prognathodon.
facts.quote: This combination of characteristics aided in determining that P. lutugini was indeed a species of Prognathodon, since some researchers place it in a genus of its own, "Dollosaurus".

facts.statement: Typical Prognathodon teeth are robust, conical, and feature blunt, serrated edges with smooth enamel.
facts.quote: Robust and conical teeth with blunt, serrated carinae and smooth enamel are often seen as typical Prognathodon teeth and are routinely assigned to the genus.

facts.statement: The type species P. solvayi possesses 12 teeth in the upper jaw and 13 in the lower jaw.
facts.quote: P. solvayi has 12 teeth on the maxilla and 13 on the dentary

facts.statement: The species P. overtoni has 14 teeth in the lower jaw.
facts.quote: P. overtoni has 14 dentary teeth.

facts.statement: P. solvayi teeth are large and strongly striated, with anterior teeth that are more forward-slanting than in any other mosasaur.
facts.quote: The tooth crowns are generally large and quite strongly striated and the anterior teeth are more procumbent than in any other mosasaurs.

facts.statement: P. solvayi tooth crowns may have been prismatic, featuring seven to eight prisms on their outer surface.
facts.quote: the tooth crowns may also have been somewhat prismatic with seven to eight prisms on the external surface.

facts.statement: The largest known tooth crowns of P. lutugini reach a height of 5.5 cm and a base width of 2.5 cm.
facts.quote: The largest known tooth crowns are up to 5.5 cm tall and 2.5 cm wide at the base.

facts.statement: Anterior pterygoid teeth in P. lutugini can be as large as 4.6 cm in height, comparable to the marginal teeth.
facts.quote: Anterior pterygoid teeth are noted for being relatively large and comparable to the marginal teeth in size at up to 4.6 cm in height.

facts.statement: The type specimen of P. lutugini preserves four cervical vertebrae with well-developed anterior and posterior zygapophyses.
facts.quote: Four cervical vertebrae are preserved, which have well-developed anterior and posterior zygapophyses.

facts.statement: The type specimen of P. lutugini preserves 26 dorsal vertebrae, although most are poorly preserved.
facts.quote: 26 dorsal vertebrae are preserved in the specimen, though most are poorly preserved.

facts.statement: The dorsal vertebrae of P. lutugini reach a maximum length of 8 cm and a height of 5 cm.
facts.quote: The dorsal vertebrae are at a maximum about 8 cm in length and 5 cm in height.

facts.statement: An exceptionally well-preserved specimen (ERMNH HFV 197) from Maastrichtian deposits in Harrana, central Jordan, provided detailed insights into the soft tissue morphology of Prognathodon.
facts.quote: The discovery of the exceptionally well-preserved specimen ERMNH HFV 197 from Maastrichtian deposits in Harrana, central Jordan allowed detailed examinations of unique details of the soft tissue morphology of Prognathodon.

facts.statement: The tail fluke of Prognathodon is similar to that of carcharhinid sharks but inverted, featuring a small upper lobe and a large lower lobe.
facts.quote: The shape of the tail fluke is similar to that of the carcharhinid sharks, though turned upside down, with a small upper lobe and large lower lobe.

facts.statement: Researchers assumed that specimen ERMNH HFV 197 was a juvenile because it was unusually small compared to other Prognathodon specimens.
facts.quote: Lindgren et al. (2013) noted that the specimen is strangely small by Prognathodon standards compared to some of the larger specimens in the genus. Thus, it was assumed that ERMNH HFV 197 was a juvenile specimen.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the upper fin lobe of Prognathodon would have grown proportionally larger in adult individuals.
facts.quote: Lindgren et al. (2013) especially noted that the upper fin lobe likely would have grown to be proportionally larger in bigger individuals.

facts.statement: Modern phylogenetic analyses place Prognathodon within the Mosasaurinae subfamily.
facts.quote: Modern phylogenetic analyses continually place Prognathodon within the Mosasaurinae subfamily

facts.statement: Gorden L. Bell Jr. recovered Prognathodon within the Mosasaurinae as a close relative of Globidens and Plesiotylosaurus.
facts.quote: Bell recovered Prognathodon within the Mosasaurinae, for the first time ever, as a close relative of the genera Globidens and Plesiotylosaurus

facts.statement: Gorden L. Bell Jr. was the first to note that Prognathodon is paraphyletic rather than monophyletic.
facts.quote: Bell was also the first to note that his analysis recovered Prognathodon, previously believed to be monophyletic, as paraphyletic
